exact_statement: For the stated N>=3 equal-dwell protocol with one zero-energy well rotating around a ring, a forward barrier lowered by d on its outgoing edge and raised by d on its incoming edge, all other wells at -A and barriers at B0, and Arrhenius rates k=nu exp[-(B-E)], every frozen phase is detailed-balanced. As tau->0, the averaged ring has u=(nu exp(-B0)/N)[exp(d)+exp(-A)(exp(-d)+N-2)] and w=(nu exp(-B0)/N)[exp(-A+d)+exp(-d)+(N-2)exp(-A)], giving J=(u-w)/N=2nu exp(-B0)(1-exp(-A))sinh(d)/N^2 and total stationary traffic T=u+w.
assumptions: instantaneous piecewise-constant protocol with equal phase duration tau
local Arrhenius rates and no unmodeled channels
high-frequency limit tau->0 at fixed finite parameters
status: internally derived conditional construction; N=3 finite Floquet/RK4 diagnostics pass; external proof audit and priority unresolved
novelty_boundary: Stochastic pumps, no-pumping, high-frequency averaging, and effective NESS currents are established. These are explicit rate/current formulas for one N-state equal-dwell protocol family; no global optimum, new general pump principle, or priority claim is made.
costs: The model requires energies, barriers, attempt rates, waveform phases, and a periodic-state solution. In the N=3 example the full period is 0.06 s and maximum phase exit rate is bounded by 1.341/s. Actuator, waveform-clock, and measurement costs are absent from the model.
falsifier: Under the specified controlled-rate model, a direct generator average or numerical Floquet solution that disagrees with u,w,J; experimentally, after model and readout calibration, failure of phase-paired controls to produce the predicted sign and approximate current rejects the mechanism for the tested system.
next_gate: Independent algebra audit; search full pump literature for the exact N-ring specialization; identify a physical state graph with measurable well/barrier modulation and chemical tight coupling.

exact_statement: For the same family in the rapid-switching limit, with work defined only as control work from state-well energy jumps and with no chemical reservoirs, state-well power is Wdot=2A nu exp(-B0)(1-exp(-A))cosh(d)/N=NA J coth(d). Eliminating d along this family yields Wdot=NA sqrt(J^2+[2nu exp(-B0)(1-exp(-A))/N^2]^2). This is an achievable family curve, not a lower bound over all protocols or total actuator-work law.
assumptions: periodic stationarity so state Shannon entropy and mean state energy return each cycle
barrier actuation and clock work omitted
net ring turns are the output variable; chemical product coupling requires an additional tight-coupling assumption
status: internally derived conditional asymptotic identity; N=3 finite-period state-well-work check agrees to about 0.035%; physical work boundary incomplete
novelty_boundary: The identification of pump work with entropy production and optimization of pump power have direct prior art; the stated N-ring formula is an internally derived specialization, with novelty unknown. It must not be presented as total energy per product.
costs: Numerical state-well work is computable from p(t) and energy jumps. Physical validation additionally needs total actuator/clock work, frequency and phase response, state occupancy/transitions, and a product coupling map.
falsifier: An algebraic contradiction under local detailed balance or a finite-period matrix-exponential result outside the stated tau->0 limit; no physical falsifier applies until a real actuator and energy boundary are specified.
next_gate: Prove or bound finite-frequency corrections for the stated family and specify an actuator model that prices barrier and clock work; then test with mirrored relative-phase controls.

exact_statement: For a prescribed periodic well waveform on a connected simple unicycle with fixed reference conductances c_e^0 and relative gate c_e=c_e^0(1+epsilon_e), the exact periodic integrated current is J_C=R_C^{-1} integral sum_e epsilon_e(q_i^epsilon-q_j^epsilon)dt, R_C=sum_e 1/c_e^0. Under |epsilon_e|<=eta<1, |J_C|<=2 eta g_max T/R_C. Linearizing around the fixed-barrier periodic state p_0 gives J_lin=R_C^{-1} integral sum_e epsilon_e D_e^0 dt, maximized to first order by epsilon_e=eta sign(D_e^0) if gates are independently controllable with no slew/bandwidth constraint. If baseline zero-sum propagators contract in l1 as M exp[-lambda(t-s)] and Lambda_0 bounds baseline escape rates, then |J_C-J_lin|<=4 M g_max Lambda_0 T eta^2/(R_C lambda) for a degree-two ring.
assumptions: connected finite graph and positive fixed reference conductances
simple unicycle for scalar cycle current and stated factor 4
periodic state for both perturbed and baseline protocols
uniform l1 mixing bound with constants M,lambda and maximum baseline escape rate Lambda_0
independent edge control and no slew restriction only for the first-order sign optimizer
status: internally reconstructed conditional control lemma; RHJ integrated-flow structure is established prior art; proof constants independently require review; numerical bound at example is valid but loose
novelty_boundary: Hodge/Laplacian current decomposition restates RHJ; the pointwise linear sign rule is elementary under an ideal actuator. The conditional quadratic remainder may be a useful certificate, but no novelty or actuator-optimality claim is established.
costs: Requires baseline well schedule and p0 or D_e^0 trace, c_e^0, T, eta, g_max, Lambda_0, and a certified or measured uniform mixing pair (M,lambda); controller must resolve each sign change. Gate and clock work are not charged.
falsifier: A counterexample satisfying the uniform contraction and rate assumptions but violating the current or remainder bound, or an independent derivation finding the Duhamel constant invalid. The first-order maximizer is falsified if admissible independent controls have an attained larger linear functional.
next_gate: Independent proof audit of Duhamel and operator-norm constants; test tightness under an explicitly bounded-bandwidth actuator and derive physical gate/clock costs.
